commitResults.messageTitle: docs: fill in student profile and add Nia's personality profile
refactor: rename chatbot from Duke to Nia
feat: implement random line selection for greetings and replies
docs: expand Nia's personality profile
feat: implement action loop with echo and formatted replies
feat: store and list user-entered tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a fixed-size array (String[100]) to store tasks so the "list"
command can echo them back, per the requirement that no more than
100 tasks need to be supported. Guards against blank input being
stored (which previously broke list's null-check termination) and
against exceeding the array's capacity.

commitResults.messageTitle: docs: note that commands are case-sensitive
commitResults.messageBody:
Clarify in the user guide that command matching is exact-case, since
the underlying implementation compares input strings directly (e.g.
"List" is not recognized as "list").

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add Task class and mark/unmark commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a Task class (description + done state) to replace the
String[] task list, so each task can carry its own status. Add
mark/unmark commands that parse a 1-indexed task number and flip its
done state, with bounds checking so an out-of-range or non-numeric
index reports an error instead of crashing.

list now iterates up to taskCount instead of scanning the full
100-slot array for a null sentinel, and the input line is trimmed
once up front so exit-command matching and word-splitting agree on
what counts as the command (previously trailing whitespace could
bypass the exit check while still being treated as a task by mistake).

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: split Nia into Ui/TaskList, flatten command handling with guard clauses
commitResults.messageBody:
refactor: split Nia into Ui/TaskList, flatten command handling

Command dispatch in main() nested up to 6 levels deep (switch -> case ->
if -> try/catch -> if), making it hard to follow. Extracted:
- Ui: all user-facing output (banners, bars, personality lines, indenting)
- TaskList: owns the task array + count instead of main() juggling both
- Nia: main() now only reads input and dispatches; each command is its
  own handleXxx() method using guard clauses instead of nested ifs

Also restyles input/reply wrapping (bars now frame the user's input line
instead of Nia's reply) and adds Javadoc to Task/Nia; see designer_log.txt

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: split input/parsing/logic/output into dedicated classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Nia.main previously mixed reading input, sanitizing it, dispatching
commands, and printing. Ui.java mixed personality voicelines with
generic output formatting. Split into:
- InputReader: raw stdin reads only
- Parser: sanitizes input into canonical words, owns command-alias
  resolution (bye/close/exit/quit -> bye), single place to add
  future aliases (e.g. dl -> deadline)
- Processor: pure command dispatch on canonical words, no
  sanitization or alias knowledge
- Printer: generic terminal output (replaces formatting half of Ui)
- VoicelineManager: personality content, prints via Printer
  (replaces personality half of Ui)

Nia.main now only orchestrates the read -> parse -> process loop.
See designer_log.txt entry 4 for full rationale.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add Todo/Deadline/Event task types with dedicated command parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
Task is now a common supertype rather than something instantiated
directly; Todo/Deadline/Event each override getTag()/toString() to add
their own tag and fields. Parser resolves td/dl aliases and splits
input into the command-specific shape each type needs (todo:
[cmd, description]; deadline: [cmd, description, by] split on "/by";
event: [cmd, description, from, to] split on "/from"/"/to"), leaving
missing fields as empty strings for Processor to validate. Processor
now rejects unrecognized commands instead of silently turning them
into tasks, and list output uses each task's toString() so the type
tag and extra fields show up.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: size printBar to terminal width
commitResults.messageBody:
Read the COLUMNS env var to make the separator bar span the terminal's
actual width instead of a hardcoded length, falling back to 100
columns when COLUMNS isn't set (e.g. non-interactive shells or IDEs).
Also switch the bar character to "─" for a cleaner look.

commitResults.messageTitle: fix: send [Debug] messages to stderr instead of stdout
commitResults.messageBody:
Debug messages were being printed through the same channel as Nia's
voicelines, making them indistinguishable when redirecting/piping
output. Adds Printer.printIndentedError() (stderr) and routes every
[Debug] message in Processor through it.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: mark Task abstract
commitResults.messageBody:
Task is only ever instantiated through its Todo/Deadline/Event
subclasses; marking it abstract makes that intent explicit and
compiler-enforced instead of just conventional.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: extract readInput() and let printStarter() frame its own bar
commitResults.messageBody:
Nia.main had the loop's bar/prompt/read/bar sequence inlined, plus a
standalone Printer.printBar() before the startup banner. Moves the
loop sequence into a named readInput() helper, and moves the startup
bar into VoicelineManager.printStarter() so the banner frames itself
the same way each prompt does. InputReader keeps its single
getUserInput() method; only import style is cleaned up (java.util.Scanner).

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: replace Parser's blank-field convention with custom exceptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Parser used to signal a missing field (todo description, /by, /from,
/to) by returning it as an empty string, leaving Processor to notice
and print the error after the fact - so the "is this valid" check was
split across two classes. Adds an abstract NiaParseException base
(carries a debug detail plus Nia's in-character voiceline) with one
concrete subclass per failure: EmptyTodoDescriptionException,
MissingDeadlineFieldsException, MissingEventFieldsException. Parser
now throws these directly, Nia.main catches NiaParseException once
around the parse step, and Processor's add-task handlers drop their
now-redundant blank checks since Parser guarantees valid fields by
the time they're called.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: split NiaException into parser/processor exception hierarchy
commitResults.messageBody:
Renamed NiaParseException to NiaParserException and pulled its
debug-message/voiceline fields up into a new abstract NiaException
root. Also adds an (as yet empty) NiaProcessorException category
alongside it, since Processor's own guard-clause errors (mark/unmark
with a non-numeric or out-of-range index) are next to convert to
exceptions and will want the same debug+voiceline handling. Splitting
into two named categories under one root lets Nia.main catch
NiaException once for uniform handling, while still leaving room to
catch a specific stage (parsing vs. processing) separately later.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: convert Processor's guard clauses to NiaProcessorException
commitResults.messageBody:
Processor's mark/unmark validation, unknown-command handling, and
full-task-list check each printed their own debug+voiceline pair
inline and returned early. Adds five NiaProcessorException subclasses
(UnknownCommandException, IncorrectMarkArgumentCountException,
NonNumericTaskIndexException, InvalidTaskIndexException,
TaskListFullException) and has Processor throw them instead.
Nia.main now wraps both Parser.parse() and Processor.process() in one
try/catch(NiaException), since every one of these failures - parser
or processor - gets the same debug-to-stderr, voiceline-to-stdout,
continue-the-loop treatment.

One behavior change: the full-task-list case now also emits a
[Debug] stderr line, matching every other error, instead of being the
only one that printed just a plain message with no debug line.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: make debug messages explain the fix, not just the failure
commitResults.messageBody:
Each exception's [Debug] message named the problem but not the
correct usage, so the user had to guess the right syntax after being
told it was wrong. Every debug message now includes a worked example
of valid input (e.g. "deadline return book /by Sunday"), and
UnknownCommandException/NonNumericTaskIndexException now echo the
actual offending value so it's clear what was rejected. Voicelines
are untouched - they stay in-character rather than instructional.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-5'
refactor: split nia package into parser, processor, ui, and content
commitResults.messageBody:
Nia.java now only holds the entry point. Parser, Processor, the
InputReader/Printer pair, and VoicelineManager each move into a
package named for their responsibility, mirroring the existing
exceptions/tasks split. A few previously package-private static
methods (Parser.parse, Processor.process, Printer's print methods,
InputReader.getUserInput, VoicelineManager's start/end voicelines)
had to become public since they're now called across package
boundaries.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: make VoicelineManager return strings instead of printing
commitResults.messageBody:
VoicelineManager previously called Printer directly, mixing content
(voicelines/banner) with output mechanics. It now only exposes getters
(getBanner, getStartingLine, getAfterRequestLine, getEndingLine), and
Nia.java composes them with Printer via new printStarter()/printEnding()
helpers, following the same pattern as the existing readInput() helper.

This keeps Printer purely mechanical, VoicelineManager purely content,
and Nia as the only place that sequences them together.

commitResults.messageTitle: docs: log the VoicelineManager/Nia orchestration refactor
commitResults.messageBody:
Appends entry 5 recording that VoicelineManager was changed from
calling Printer directly to returning plain strings, with Nia.java
gaining printStarter()/printEnding() helpers to do the composition.

commitResults.messageTitle: docs: write the user guide from the placeholder template
commitResults.messageBody:
Replaces the template's TODO comments with real documentation for
todo/deadline/event, list, mark/unmark, bye, and the current command
aliases (close/exit/quit, td, dl) - derived from Processor and Parser
so the examples and output formats match actual behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: back TaskList with ArrayList instead of a fixed-size array
commitResults.messageBody:
Drops the fixed-capacity constructor and isFull() check, since ArrayList
grows on its own. This makes TaskListFullException (and its throws clauses
in Processor) dead code, so it's removed along with them.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: add ls/list alias, quote added-task message, lowercase event labels
feat: add delete command with "d" alias
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds TaskList.delete(index) and a Processor handler that removes the task
and echoes it back with the remaining count, in Nia's voice. Generalizes
IncorrectMarkArgumentCountException into IncorrectTaskIndexArgumentCountException
and factors the "parse + validate a single task-index argument" logic out
of handleMarkOrUnmark into a shared helper, since mark/unmark/delete all
take the same single-index argument shape.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add save-format serialization to Task hierarchy
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds toSaveFormat(), overridden per subclass the same way toString()
already is, producing the |~|-delimited on-disk format (e.g.
"D|~|1|~|finish math homework|~|Wednesday 6PM"). Also adds a public
isDone() getter so callers outside the tasks package can read
completion state without touching the internal field.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add Storage for loading/saving tasks to disk
commitResults.messageBody:
Reads/writes ./data/nia.txt in the |~|-delimited format. load()
returns an empty TaskList if the file doesn't exist, and skips
malformed lines with a warning rather than crashing startup. save()
rewrites the whole file, which is simplest and correct at this scale.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: made TaskList load() on startup, file now updates after every command
commitResults.messageBody:
Loads tasks from disk at startup via Storage.load() instead of
starting with an empty TaskList, and saves after every processed
command so state survives even if the process is killed rather than
exited cleanly via "bye".

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-6'
Sync branch 'master' into branch-Level-7
fix: adapt Storage to the merged ArrayList-backed TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
Master's merge dropped TaskList's fixed-capacity array constructor for
an unbounded ArrayList (and added delete). Storage.load(int capacity)
no longer had anything to size, so it drops the parameter and calls
the no-arg TaskList() constructor; Nia.java updated to match. No
change needed for delete itself - save() already rewrites the file
from taskList's current contents on every command, so a deletion is
picked up on the next save automatically.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-7'
refactor: move task-index parsing from Processor into Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
parseAndValidateTaskIndex (shared by mark/unmark/delete) validates that
a command's argument is a well-formed, in-range task number - that is
input validation, the same job Parser already does for todo/deadline/
event's required fields. Having it live in Processor meant task-index
validation was split across two classes for no reason.

Processor's mark/unmark/delete handlers now call
Parser.parseAndValidateTaskIndex instead of a private copy of the same
method. No behavior change; exception types are unchanged for now.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: fix exception hierarchy after task-index parsing moved to Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
IncorrectTaskIndexArgumentCountException, InvalidTaskIndexException,
and NonNumericTaskIndexException now extend NiaParserException instead
of NiaProcessorException. They're thrown from Parser.parseAndValidate
TaskIndex (moved there in the previous commit), and the doc comments
on NiaException/NiaParserException/NiaProcessorException define the
split strictly by which stage throws - turning input into words vs.
acting on those words - so leaving them under NiaProcessorException
contradicted that.

Parser.parseAndValidateTaskIndex now declares 'throws NiaParserException'
to match.

Processor.process/handleMarkOrUnmark/handleDelete widen from
'throws NiaProcessorException' to 'throws NiaException', since they
now propagate both a genuine NiaProcessorException (UnknownCommandException)
and the reclassified NiaParserException subtypes. Nia.java needs no
change, since it already catches the common NiaException root.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master' into branch-Level-8
feat: add date-time parsing/formatting helpers to Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds parseDateTime (tries every accepted input format - '-' or '/' date
separator, optional HHmm/HH:mm time defaulting to 23:59), formatCanonical/
parseCanonical (round-trip through the one save-file format), and
formatDisplay (friendly 'Oct 15 2019, 6:00pm' style) as new static
methods on Parser, alongside the existing parseAndValidateTaskIndex.

New InvalidDateTimeException (extends NiaParserException, matching every
other parser-stage failure) for when none of the accepted formats match.

Nothing calls these yet - parseDeadline/parseEvent still pass by/from/to
through unvalidated. This is purely additive so the build stays green;
wiring it in is the next commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: program now rejects invalid date-time formats
commitResults.messageBody:
parseDeadline/parseEvent now run the extracted by/from/to substring
through parseDateTime (added last commit) after the existing blank-check,
and store the result back in canonical format via formatCanonical. A
value that doesn't match any accepted format now throws
InvalidDateTimeException instead of silently passing through as free
text. Both methods widen their throws clause from their specific
Missing...FieldsException to NiaParserException, since two exception
types can now come out.

Deadline/Event/Processor/Storage are untouched - they still treat
by/from/to as plain Strings, just always a validated, canonical-format
one now. Manually verified: valid dates (with/without time, both date
separators) are accepted and normalized; invalid ones are rejected with
the new voiceline; old free-text save data still loads (Storage doesn't
validate on load yet - that's next).

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: switch deadline/event date storage from String to LocalDateTime
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline.by and Event.from/to are now LocalDateTime instead of String,
with getters added. toString() uses Parser.formatDisplay for a friendly
'Oct 15 2019, 6:00pm' style; toSaveFormat() uses Parser.formatCanonical
for the lossless save-file format.

Processor.handleAddDeadline/handleAddEvent and Storage.parseLine's D/E
cases now convert the canonical string (guaranteed valid since the
previous commit) via Parser.parseCanonical before constructing
Deadline/Event.

Bug found and fixed along the way: DateTimeParseException extends
DateTimeException -> RuntimeException directly, NOT
IllegalArgumentException as assumed - so Storage.parseLine's existing
catch (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException | IllegalArgumentException) did
NOT cover it. Old free-text save data (e.g. '12/9/2026') crashed the
whole app on load instead of being skipped as a corrupted line. Added
DateTimeParseException to the catch clause.

Manually verified: display format, save-file format, and a full
save/reload round-trip all work; old-format save lines are now skipped
with a warning instead of crashing.

commitResults.messageTitle: docs: document date-time format, log the LocalDateTime refactor
commitResults.messageBody:
docs/README.md: replaced deadline/event examples with valid dates
matching the newly-enforced format, added a Date-time format section
documenting the accepted patterns and the 23:59 default. Also fixed a
stale example while touching this section - the event output showed
capitalized 'FROM:'/'TO:', but the code has always lowercased it.

designer_log.txt: appended a 6th entry in the existing 'Changed FROM
... TO ... / Reason: ...' format, covering the String -> LocalDateTime
change across Parser/Deadline/Event/Processor/Storage and the
DateTimeParseException catch-clause bug found during manual testing.

data/nia.txt (the sample save file) is gitignored, not tracked - so
there's nothing to commit there despite the original plan calling for
it; the old free-text lines in it are simply skipped as corrupted on
load, per Storage's existing behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: build: add Gson dependency
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds com.google.code.gson:gson:2.14.0 (current stable) as a main
implementation dependency - the next few commits replace Storage's
hand-rolled pipe-delimited text format with JSON via Gson.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add Gson adapter for LocalDateTime
commitResults.messageBody:
LocalDateTimeJsonAdapter teaches Gson how to (de)serialize LocalDateTime,
a type it has no built-in support for. Stored as a plain ISO-8601 string
via LocalDateTime's own toString()/parse() (e.g. '2019-10-15T18:00:00') -
no custom pattern needed, standard for JSON.

Not wired into anything yet (Storage still uses the old text format) -
this is purely additive so the build stays green.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add Gson adapter for Task's polymorphism
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskJsonAdapter teaches Gson how to (de)serialize the abstract Task -
Gson's default reflection-based handling can't know which concrete
subclass (Todo/Deadline/Event) a bare Task field should become on the
way back in. Adds a 'type' field to the JSON (full word, independent
of Task#getTag()'s display-only single-letter 'T'/'D'/'E') and
dispatches on it when deserializing.

Deadline/Event's by/from/to fields are delegated through
context.serialize/deserialize(..., LocalDateTime.class) rather than
formatting them directly, so this adapter doesn't need to know how
LocalDateTime.class's own adapter (added last commit) represents them.

Not wired into anything yet (Storage still uses the old text format) -
this is purely additive so the build stays green.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: switch Storage from pipe-delimited text to JSON
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage now reads/writes data/nia.json (a pretty-printed JSON array of
tasks) via a Gson instance registered with TaskJsonAdapter and
LocalDateTimeJsonAdapter (added in the last two commits), instead of
hand-rolled pipe-delimited parsing/formatting. load()/save() are now a
single gson.fromJson/toJson call each.

Task.toSaveFormat()/SAVE_DELIMITER and Deadline/Event's toSaveFormat()
overrides are removed - dead code now that Gson's reflection-based
serialization replaces them entirely.

Bug found and fixed during manual testing, same shape as the one from
the LocalDateTime migration: Storage.load()'s catch clause needs
JsonParseException (covers both Gson's own syntax errors and the
'unknown type' case TaskJsonAdapter throws - note JsonSyntaxException
alone would miss the latter), DateTimeParseException (a separate
RuntimeException hierarchy, thrown by LocalDateTimeJsonAdapter), AND
NullPointerException (a task object missing an expected field
entirely, e.g. hand-edited) - without all three, a corrupted save file
crashes the app instead of being skipped.

Manually verified: fresh add of one of each task type produces the
expected JSON schema; mark + restart round-trips done-state and dates
correctly; a syntactically invalid file, a bad date-time string, and
an unknown 'type' value are all now handled by warning and starting
fresh instead of crashing.

commitResults.messageTitle: docs: log the JSON storage migration
commitResults.messageBody:
Appends a 7th entry to designer_log.txt in the existing 'Changed FROM
... TO ... / Reason: ...' format, covering the pipe-delimited -> JSON
switch, the two new Gson adapters, the toSaveFormat() removal, and the
three-exception-type catch clause bug found during manual testing.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add UnknownListFilterException for bad list filter tokens
commitResults.messageBody:
Thrown by the upcoming list-filter parsing when the t//d//e/ token
after 'list' doesn't match a known alias (task/todo, dl/deadline, event).

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: parse t//d//e/ filter tokens after the list command
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds Parser.parseList/resolveListFilterTag so 'list t/task', 'list d/dl'
or 'list d/deadline', and 'list e/event' resolve to the same tag letters
(T/D/E) Task.getTag() already returns, instead of being silently dropped
by the generic whitespace-split fallback. Invalid tokens now throw
UnknownListFilterException rather than being ignored.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: filter list output by task type while keeping full-list indices
commitResults.messageBody:
handleList now reads the optional tag from words[1] and skips
non-matching tasks, but keeps looping i over the full list so printed
indices still match what mark/unmark/delete expect, even when filtered.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add EmptyFindKeywordException for a bare find command
commitResults.messageBody:
Thrown by the upcoming find-keyword parsing when 'find' is given no
keyword, mirroring EmptyTodoDescriptionException's shape.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: parse the find command's keyword argument
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds Parser.parseFind, mirroring parseTodo: rejects a blank keyword
(via EmptyFindKeywordException) and otherwise returns [command, rest]
so the raw search text reaches Processor unmodified.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: implement find as a case-insensitive description search
commitResults.messageBody:
handleFind loops the full task list and prints entries whose
description contains words[1] (case-insensitive), keeping i as the
full-list index so results stay usable with mark/unmark/delete -
same approach as the filtered list command.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add a help command listing all available commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Prints a quick-reference summary of every command Processor recognizes
(list, todo, deadline, event, mark, unmark, delete, find, help, bye)
and their argument syntax, so users don't need to guess or dig through
docs to see what's available.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: accept plain words as list filter tokens instead of slash form
commitResults.messageBody:
Change the list filter syntax from slash-prefixed tokens (t/todo, d/dl,
d/deadline, e/event) to plain words (t, todo, d, dl, deadline, e, event),
matched case-insensitively. The old slash form wasn't intuitive - most
users typed "list t" or "list deadline" and got rejected. Also drops the
"t/task" alias, since "t" selects todos, not a generic "task" type.
